learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic concepts of applied magnetism.
Understand and provide explanation for the basic properties of hard and soft magnetic materials.
Propose methods for characterization of different magnetic materials.
Discuss various applications of nanomagnetic materials in cutting edge technologies and devices.
Acquire experience in collecting information on special topics of micro/nanomagnetism and be in a position to conduct research in the field.
Development of interdisciplinary and critical thinking.
Search for, analysis and synthesis of data and information, with the use of the necessary tools.
Production of free, creative and inductive thinking.

syllabus_topics: Types of magnetic order- Magnetic domains

assessment_methods.method: Final written examination (combination of short-answer questions, problem solving, theory questions)

assessment_rules: The evaluation includes an optional test, a written report on a project selected by the student from a list, and a final written examination. The final examination includes a combination of short-answer questions, problem solving, and theory questions requiring a topic development. Students retain the right to view their exam scripts after grades are published and ask questions.
bibliography: J.M.D. Coey, “Magnetism and Magnetic Materials”, Cambridge Univ. Press, Greek translation: Public City (2012).
D. Jiles, “Introduction to Magnetism and Magnetic Materials”, Chapman & Hall (1991).
C. Kittel, “Introduction to Solid State Physics”, Wiley, Greek translation: Pnevmatikos Publishing (1976).
Journal of magnetism and magnetic materials
degree: Materials Science and Engineering — Πτυχίο Τμήματος Επιστήμης και Μηχανικής Υλικών (first cycle, 240 ECTS, curriculum ΕΜΥ)
